narration: We begin with the content reference. A photo of a cat is handled by the Content LoRA, a pair of low-rank matrices B and A.
Below it, the style reference, a Van Gogh style painting, has its own Style LoRA with the same B and A structure.
Each branch collapses into its low-rank product, B times A, and both products are fed forward into the fusion module.
That module is K-LoRA. Layer by layer, it decides whether content or style should take the lead.
Inside, it looks at the content branch's attention map and sums its Top-K largest elements.
It does exactly the same for the style branch, summing the Top-K elements of the style attention map.
The style sum is first multiplied by a scale factor, which tunes how strongly style competes against content.
The Judge then compares the two sums and selects whichever branch has the bigger Top-K response at this layer.
The winner becomes the attention layer that is actually used: the one with the bigger Top-K.
Its output is added to the current latent feature map at the add node.
The merged features go back into the diffusion UNet, where the selected attention layer is applied during denoising.
The result is the content cat rendered in the style of the reference painting.
